# The neuralLink fixture stops the Bridge it spawned

## Context

defect-note 2026-10-17 17:46Z (fingerprint `7aa4bc2640663fdc`). The Neural Link Bridge that the Engine's `neuralLink` Playwright fixture spawns outlives the run. A Stage e2e run at 17:04Z started its Bridge (`npm run ai:server-neural-link` from `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`) on `NEO_NL_PORT` 18981; 31 minutes later it was still listening, and the next run found the port taken. The same happened after the 17:3xZ run. Both were stopped by exact PID.

With hosted Stage CI off until the Nov 1 reset, authors run the e2e tiers locally on the operator's machine (operator directive, relayed 2026-10-17 16:58Z; local testing is priority zero). Every run leaves a Bridge behind there.

Emmy's source triage (A2A 17:54Z), re-read here:
- `test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:261` starts the Bridge (`manageConnection({action: 'start'})`), and the fixture ends at `await use(nl)` (`:861`) with no `finally` and no stop.
- In the Brain, `ConnectionService.manageConnection` with `action: 'stop'` kills only its own `bridgeProcess` (`ai/services/neural-link/ConnectionService.mjs:913–923`, `bridgeProcess.kill()`).
- That process is the `npm` parent of a `detached` spawn (`:1037–1039`). Whether killing it reaps the `node run-bridge.mjs` child is not shown.

## The Problem

A local e2e run leaves a Bridge process and a bound port per run. A later run on the same port connects to whatever is listening, which can be a Bridge started from another `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`, so it may run other Brain code than the run requested. No current spec observes any of this.

## The Architectural Reality

- `neuralLink` (`test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:244`) is test-scoped. The first test of a worker spawns the Bridge when none is listening; the later tests connect to it. A per-test stop would respawn a Bridge for every test, so the stop belongs at worker end.
- The fixture is the second Bridge entrypoint, beside the MCP server (`:257`). A Bridge the fixture found running belongs to someone else, such as the operator's live `:8081` or another seat's, and must not be stopped.
- The fixture ships in the `neo.mjs` package. Stage and the Institution import it from `node_modules/neo.mjs/test/playwright/fixtures.mjs`, so they receive the fix with the Engine version they pin.

## The Fix

Move the Bridge lifecycle into a worker-scoped fixture (`{scope: 'worker'}`) that the test-scoped `neuralLink` depends on. Once per worker it starts or connects, and records whether this worker spawned the Bridge. After `use`, it stops only a Bridge it spawned, through the Brain's stop contract, never one it found running. If the witness shows that the Brain's stop leaves the `node` child alive, the reaping belongs to `ConnectionService`, which owns the spawn. That gap becomes a Brain leaf with the witness; the fixture does not kill around it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1: On an initially unused port, a run that spawned the Bridge leaves no listener and no process from that spawn once its worker ends.
- [x] AC-2: The same holds when a test in the run fails.
- [x] AC-3: A Bridge already listening on the port before the run is used and left running (the external-Bridge control).
- [x] AC-4: The PR records the witness for AC-1–AC-3: PID, process group and port, before and after. If the Brain's stop does not reap the child, the PR names the Brain leaf it filed.

## Out of Scope

- `ConnectionService`'s own stop semantics (a Brain leaf if AC-4 finds a gap).
- Consumers' pin bumps.
- The MCP server's Bridge lifecycle.
